title: Boolean games
description: In a Boolean game each player controls some variables and wants a goal formula to be true; an assignment is a pure Nash equilibrium if no player whose goal is false can make it true alone, and existence is Sigma-2-complete (Bonzon, Lagasquie-Schiex, Lang and Zanuttini). The check guesses a player and a profitable deviation, which depends on why the goal fails now and on the other players' literals that the new goal needs. Four of the six equilibria make everybody win; in two, one player loses and cannot help it.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The players, their variables and their goals. Added to every solver.
fragments.text: % The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): assignments to all variables.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a strategy profile, that is, a value for every variable.
{ t(V) } :- var(V).
#show t/1.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the values of the variables.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a player with a profitable deviation (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: one player deviates ...
1 { dev(P) : player(P) } 1.
own(V) :- dev(P), controls(P,V).
% ... its goal is false now: some clause of the goal is false (the first one is noted) ...
now(C) :- pos(C,V), t(V).
now(C) :- neg(C,V), not t(V).
broken(C) :- dev(P), goal(P,C), not now(C).
lost :- broken(C).
:- not lost.
% ... and true after it changes its own variables (n/1 is the new assignment).
{ n(V) } :- own(V).
n(V) :- t(V), not own(V).
mine(C)   :- pos(C,V), own(V), n(V).
mine(C)   :- neg(C,V), own(V), not n(V).
others(C) :- pos(C,V), not own(V), t(V).
others(C) :- neg(C,V), not own(V), not t(V).
:- dev(P), goal(P,C), not mine(C), not others(C).
#show dev/1.
#show n/1.

% What the deviation depends on:
% - the first broken clause stays false: all its variables keep their values;
witness(C) :- broken(C), not broken(D) : goal(_,D), D < C.
relevant(t(V)) :- witness(C), pos(C,V).
relevant(t(V)) :- witness(C), neg(C,V).
% - a goal clause that the player's new values do not satisfy is satisfied by the
%   others: their literals that are true in it keep their values.
relevant(t(V)) :- dev(P), goal(P,C), not mine(C), pos(C,V), not own(V), t(V).
relevant(t(V)) :- dev(P), goal(P,C), not mine(C), neg(C,V), not own(V), not t(V).

fragments.name: check_others
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: one player deviates ...
1 { dev(P) : player(P) } 1.
own(V) :- dev(P), controls(P,V).
% ... its goal is false now: some clause of the goal is false (the first one is noted) ...
now(C) :- pos(C,V), t(V).
now(C) :- neg(C,V), not t(V).
broken(C) :- dev(P), goal(P,C), not now(C).
lost :- broken(C).
:- not lost.
% ... and true after it changes its own variables (n/1 is the new assignment).
{ n(V) } :- own(V).
n(V) :- t(V), not own(V).
mine(C)   :- pos(C,V), own(V), n(V).
mine(C)   :- neg(C,V), own(V), not n(V).
others(C) :- pos(C,V), not own(V), t(V).
others(C) :- neg(C,V), not own(V), not t(V).
:- dev(P), goal(P,C), not mine(C), not others(C).
#show dev/1.
#show n/1.

% A coarser refinement: the first broken clause keeps its values, and so does every
% variable that the deviating player does not control.
witness(C) :- broken(C), not broken(D) : goal(_,D), D < C.
relevant(t(V)) :- witness(C), pos(C,V).
relevant(t(V)) :- witness(C), neg(C,V).
relevant(t(V)) :- var(V), not own(V).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts:
% A Boolean game: four players, each controls two variables and wants its own goal
% (a formula in clause form) to be true.
player(1..4).
var(1..8).
controls(P,2*P-1) :- player(P).
controls(P,2*P)   :- player(P).
% goal(P,C): clause C belongs to the goal of player P; pos(C,V) / neg(C,V): its literals.
goal(1,11). pos(11,2). neg(11,6).                 % v2 | ~v6
goal(1,12). neg(12,1). neg(12,3).                 % ~v1 | ~v3
goal(1,13). neg(13,1). pos(13,3). pos(13,4).      % ~v1 | v3 | v4
goal(2,21). pos(21,1). pos(21,3). pos(21,7).      % v1 | v3 | v7
goal(2,22). pos(22,4). pos(22,6).                 % v4 | v6
goal(2,23). pos(23,2). neg(23,3). neg(23,4).      % v2 | ~v3 | ~v4
goal(3,31). neg(31,4). neg(31,5).                 % ~v4 | ~v5
goal(3,32). neg(32,4). pos(32,5). pos(32,6).      % ~v4 | v5 | v6
goal(3,33). pos(33,7). pos(33,8).                 % v7 | v8
goal(4,41). neg(41,6). neg(41,7).                 % ~v6 | ~v7
goal(4,42). neg(42,3). pos(42,8).                 % ~v3 | v8
goal(4,43). pos(43,6). pos(43,7).                 % v6 | v7

% Matching pennies: player 1 wants v1 = v2, player 2 wants v1 != v2. No equilibrium.
player(1;2).
var(1;2).
controls(1,1). controls(2,2).
goal(1,11). pos(11,1). neg(11,2).                 % v1 | ~v2
goal(1,12). neg(12,1). pos(12,2).                 % ~v1 | v2
goal(2,21). pos(21,1). pos(21,2).                 % v1 | v2
goal(2,22). neg(22,1). neg(22,2).                 % ~v1 | ~v2

% A coordination game: three players, each controls one variable and all want v1 = v2 = v3.
% Two equilibria; in every other profile one player is the odd one out and can switch.
player(1..3).
var(1..3).
controls(P,P) :- player(P).
goal(P,10*P+1) :- player(P).  pos(10*P+1,1) :- player(P).  neg(10*P+1,2) :- player(P).   % v1 | ~v2
goal(P,10*P+2) :- player(P).  neg(10*P+2,1) :- player(P).  pos(10*P+2,2) :- player(P).   % ~v1 | v2
goal(P,10*P+3) :- player(P).  pos(10*P+3,2) :- player(P).  neg(10*P+3,3) :- player(P).   % v2 | ~v3
goal(P,10*P+4) :- player(P).  neg(10*P+4,2) :- player(P).  pos(10*P+4,3) :- player(P).   % ~v2 | v3

% Three players with two variables each; each goal mentions another player's variables.
player(1..3).
var(1..6).
controls(P,2*P-1) :- player(P).
controls(P,2*P)   :- player(P).
goal(1,11). pos(11,1). pos(11,3).                 % v1 | v3
goal(1,12). neg(12,2). neg(12,5).                 % ~v2 | ~v5
goal(2,21). neg(21,3). pos(21,6).                 % ~v3 | v6
goal(2,22). pos(22,4). neg(22,1).                 % v4 | ~v1
goal(3,31). neg(31,5). neg(31,4).                 % ~v5 | ~v4
goal(3,32). pos(32,6). pos(32,2).                 % v6 | v2

generators.name: random-game
generators.description: A random Boolean game: p players with two variables each; every goal is g clauses of k distinct literals over all variables, signs with probability 1/2.
generators.text:
% boolean-game: p players, each controls two variables; each goal has g clauses of k distinct literals.
player(1..p).
var(1..2*p).
controls(P,2*P-1) :- player(P).
controls(P,2*P) :- player(P).
goal(P,10*P+J) :- player(P), J = 1..g.
inl(C,X) :- goal(P,C), var(X), @subset(k, 2*p, X, C) = 1.
pos(C,X) :- inl(C,X), @flip(500, C, X) = 1.
neg(C,X) :- inl(C,X), @flip(500, C, X) = 0.
#show player/1.  #show var/1.  #show controls/2.  #show goal/2.  #show pos/2.  #show neg/2.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 5):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + abstraction   options "--enum-mode=record"
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

spaces.name: games
spaces.description: Two players, size variables, one goal clause per player.
spaces.text:
% every two-player game over the variables 1..size: who controls what, one goal clause each
player(1..2).  var(1..size).
1 { controls(P,V) : player(P) } 1 :- var(V).
goal(P,P) :- player(P).
{ pos(C,V) : player(C), var(V) }.
{ neg(C,V) : player(C), var(V) }.
